# OrgPath — Governance {.unnumbered}

**OrgPath** is the governance member of the Org family — the operational
expression of the UIAO substrate that makes *canon the source of truth*.
Schemas, registries, and policies form a protected corpus where every
governance claim traces to a certificate-anchored origin: no backfilling,
no orphan claims. Its addressing primitives — **OrgTree** (organizational
hierarchy), **OrgPath** (the attribute path itself), and **LocPath**
(location addressing) — give every identity, device, and policy a governed
address.

**OrgPath** governs, **OrgComp** proves federal organizational compliance,
**OrgMod** modernizes — three expressions of one substrate, adoptable
together or entirely independently.

## What OrgPath governs

- **The addressing plane** — [OrgTree](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/orgtree.qmd)
  and [LocPath](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/locpath.qmd) as a
  single coordinated namespace, with the
  [codebook](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/codebook.qmd) binding
  paths to authoritative codes.
- **Drift** — the
  [drift walkthrough](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/drift-walkthrough.qmd)
  shows the closed loop: scan, classify, remediate, verify.
- **Delegation and dynamic membership** —
  [delegation](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/delegation.qmd) and
  [dynamic groups](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/dynamic-groups.qmd)
  derived from the governed path instead of hand-curated lists.
- **Portability** — the
  [portability model](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/orgpath-portability.qmd)
  keeps the namespace vendor-neutral across directory and cloud stacks.

## One lifecycle, three pillars {#macdr}

Every operational change the Org family touches — every **Move, Add, Change,
Deletion, and Reset (MACD-R)** — travels the same five-clause authorized
path: **it originates with the SSOT → carries an authoritative authorization
→ executes under least privilege with just-in-time elevation (PIM) → closes
with provenance → emits verified, secured evidence automatically to
continuous monitoring.** OrgPath applies the law to identity and attribute
governance: a joiner, mover, or leaver event in the HR source of truth is
the only thing that originates an identity change, and the closure evidence
carries that SSOT lineage back to reporting. The full doctrine — including
Closure Provenance ("no closure counts unless it carries its proof") — is
stated in
[OrgComp Vol 0 Book 00](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/Vol_0_Book_00_OrgComp_Executive_Summary.qmd#macdr-lifecycle).
